stories.title: The Trump administration is supporting OpenAI in the NYT copyright lawsuit

bullet_points: The Trump administration has officially intervened in the NYT's copyright lawsuit against OpenAI.

The intervention signals a high-level political involvement in a landmark legal battle over AI data usage and intellectual property.

stories.title: Google dodges another breakup attempt
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: A US District Court Judge declined the Justice Department's request for Google to sell off parts of its ad tech business.
The court accepted milder, behavioral remedies instead of a forced breakup to address alleged monopolization.
The judge will adopt most proposed behavioral changes, though some modifications will be made.

stories.title: US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: US court ruled against Google in an antitrust case concerning its ad exchange.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) successfully proved Google acted illegally.
However, the court declined to mandate that Google sell its ad exchange, limiting the DOJ's desired outcome.

stories.title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
stories.author: Fernanda González, wired.com
bullet_points: The U.S. Army has deployed a 20-kilowatt laser system.
This technology is designed to track and neutralize hostile drones.
The successful use demonstrates a significant advancement in directed energy weapons for defense.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback mechanism for improving language agents.
VRL allows for the conveyance of complex information like intent, preferences, and causal structure in a human-interpretable format.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Facet-0, a new robotic foundation model designed for high-precision, contact-rich manipulation tasks.
The model integrates multimodal representation learning and reinforcement learning to predict and value contact consequences.
It unifies causal wrench history with vision-language semantics and kinematic state for robust action planning.

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: The research investigates the uneven accuracy degradation caused by Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
It proposes a method to intelligently allocate a limited additional precision budget to mitigate quantization damage across different model layers.
The study validates its findings across nine open-weight models spanning four different architectural families using causal mixed-precision intervention.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a new paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback channel for improving language agents.
VRL allows language models to receive feedback conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in a human-interpretable way.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what specific aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
stories.author: bratao
bullet_points: Announcement of Gemini 3.8 Flash, indicating an update to Google's Gemini model family.

stories.author: donohoe
bullet_points: Google successfully defended against a US bid to force the breakup or sale of its ad tech business.
The legal outcome suggests a significant regulatory hurdle for antitrust actions against Google's advertising ecosystem.
This development has major implications for the future structure and market dominance of large tech platforms.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama

stories.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Amazon is integrating AI into its assistant to detect impersonation scams.
The feature allows users to verify if emails, texts, or calls genuinely originate from Amazon.
Users can query Alexa about suspicious messages to leverage the AI's verification capabilities.

stories.title: Wary of Artemis IV timeline, NASA is changing lunar spacesuit design
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is modifying the design of the lunar spacesuit.

bullet_points: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, marking the third Flash model release in six weeks.

The news is noted in the context of a perceived pause in updates to Google's Pro model.

stories.title: Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Trump's reviews of frontier AI models may conceal corruption.
The core issue revolves around the transparency of federal AI safety testing rules.
The potential forced revelation of secret federal AI safety protocols is the central conflict.

stories.title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses potential failures within Rassvet, a satellite system positioned as a rival to Starlink.
Initial data suggests at least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites have experienced outright failures.
The news touches upon the competitive landscape of satellite internet constellations.

stories.title: BGP hijack infecting networks caused by a comedy of errors that’s not funny at all
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A BGP hijacking incident successfully poisoned production software.
The incident was attributed to a 'comedy of errors' rather than malicious intent.
The event serves as a case study for learning about BGP security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces PTA-IRT, a new framework for benchmarking software engineering (SWE) agents.
Addresses the high cost of evaluating SWE agents by moving beyond simple pass/fail metrics.
PTA-IRT is 'Trajectory-Aware,' meaning it evaluates *how* agents solve problems, not just the final outcome.

stories.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of generating code consistent with large, real-world code repositories.
Proposes an 'Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval' method to overcome LLM input length limitations.
Improves upon standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by providing more granular, repository-specific context.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark for testing language model reasoning.
Focuses on the complex problem of component lifecycle reasoning within dynamic agent harnesses.
Addresses the challenge where local software changes can propagate through dependencies and require careful cleanup.

stories.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
stories.author: Stephen Morris
bullet_points: Presents a mechanism design framework for controlling AI agents with unknown preferences and capabilities.
The framework aims to incentivize AI agents to be both honest and obedient when acting on behalf of a designer.
Introduces a 'revelation principle' based on a one-sided imitation structure, characterizing implementable policies.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research focuses on developing 'proactive thought partners' for writing, moving beyond simple autocomplete.
These AI agents aim to provide customizable, higher-level cognitive support tailored to the writer's needs at specific moments.
The paper explores the design space for such proactive AI assistance across the entire writing process (ideation to revision).

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open research problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by developing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency and brittleness of using large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly as decision-making policies.
Introduces SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), a framework to learn a cheap, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
The core mechanism involves selectively querying the VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty.

stories.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification
stories.author: Jayasimha Talur
bullet_points: The paper addresses a known limitation of LLMs: difficulty in classifying text into taxonomies with many semantically similar, domain-specific labels.
Current solutions relying on top-K retrieval of candidate labels fail because they do not help the model differentiate between highly similar options.
The proposed method introduces 'Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection' to improve classification accuracy in complex, fine-grained label spaces.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the internal mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used to evaluate Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
It employs an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy to mechanistically probe how LLMs assign ratings across Readability and Adequacy dimensions.
The research addresses the lack of understanding regarding how LLM evaluators function when used as automated scoring tools or training signals.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal resource allocation ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: The research addresses the high cost and brittleness of using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly for interactive decision-making.
A new framework, SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), is proposed to learn a cheap, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
SAGE intelligently queries the VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty, improving efficiency.

stories.title: Gradient-Update Mismatch: Rethinking Conflict-Free Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
stories.author: Tiejun Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical challenge in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs): conflicting gradients arising from jointly optimizing physics residuals and boundary conditions.
It introduces 'gradient surgery' methods to construct conflict-free directions from loss-specific gradients to reduce training conflicts.
A key limitation identified is that the conflict-free property achieved by gradient surgery may not be maintained after standard optimizer transformations.

stories.title: Can LLMs Discover Scientific Laws in Real and Parallel Worlds?
stories.author: Jingbo Shang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the open question of whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can genuinely discover scientific laws.
Scientific discovery traditionally involves iterative cycles of hypothesis generation, testing, and refinement.
Current evaluations of LLM discovery capabilities are often limited, either using synthetic data or reusing existing published work.

stories.title: A Mathematical Theory of Reusable Neural Bases for Network Compression
stories.author: Binshuai Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the critical bottleneck of memory cost in large AI models during training and inference.
Introduces the Linear Reusable Neural Bases Architecture (LRNBA) to improve parameter efficiency.
The core concept involves representing network blocks as a linear combination of a shared set of bases, inspired by RNN designs.

stories.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Viliam Lisý
bullet_points: Introduces NashDreamer, a novel Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) approach.
Addresses the challenge of applying MBRL to competitive Imperfect-Information Games (IIGs).
Argues for the necessity of centralized model learning to overcome non-stationarity and identifiability issues in multi-agent settings.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the opaque internal mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used to evaluate Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
It introduces an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy to mechanistically probe how LLMs assign ratings across Readability and Adequacy dimensions.
This research addresses a critical gap in current NLP evaluation practices where LLM scoring procedures are poorly understood.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Proposes PTA-IRT, a new framework for evaluating Software Engineering (SWE) agents.
Addresses the high cost of evaluating SWE agents on realistic, multi-step tasks.
Moves beyond simple result-only evaluation by incorporating trajectory-aware analysis of how agents solve problems.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark for testing language model reasoning.
Focuses on the complex lifecycle reasoning required when language models dynamically alter their own execution environments (agent harnesses).
Addresses the challenge of tracking dependency propagation and cleanup when components are modified at runtime.

stories.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: StudentSim proposes using LLM-based student simulators to gather data on effective AI tutoring strategies.
Current simulation methods are limited: state-tracking models lack explanatory depth, while LLM role-play lacks competence matching.
The research addresses the need for scalable, low-cost methods to determine personalized guidance for AI tutors.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing 'proactive thought partners' for writing, moving beyond basic autocomplete.
These AI agents aim to offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support tailored to the writer's needs at specific moments.
The paper explores the design space for AI that assists with diverse writing activities, from ideation to revision.

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: The paper investigates the uneven accuracy degradation caused by Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
It proposes a method to strategically allocate a limited additional precision budget to mitigate quantization damage.
The research tests hypotheses across 9 open-weight models and 4 architecture families using causal mixed-precision intervention.

stories.title: Closing Cost-Quality Gap in Document VLMs: Difficulty-Aware Data Curation and Quality-Adjusted Deployment Economics
stories.author: Aleksandr Ivanov
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost and quality gap in using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for extracting structured data from massive document volumes in regulated industries.
Proposes a deployed system utilizing a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLM architecture (35B total, 3B active) fine-tuned on proprietary and open-domain data.
Tackles practical deployment challenges, specifically making the model cost-effective enough to compete with traditional human annotation methods while adhering to privacy constraints.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Streamline Publishing with a Claude Code Skill
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: Introduces a Claude Code skill designed to automate content syndication from a single Markdown file.
The skill generates optimized versions for multiple platforms (Dev.to, AWS Builder Center, Medium, LinkedIn).
It includes pre-shipping checks and debugging tools to ensure cross-platform consistency.

stories.title: Execution Trees, Not More Logs: A Better Debugging Model for AI Agents
stories.author: raju_dandigam
bullet_points: Proposes 'Execution Trees' as a superior debugging model for AI agents.
Critiques traditional flat logging methods for their inability to pinpoint causal operations.
Addresses a core challenge in complex AI system observability and debugging.

stories.title: I Found 3 Security Vulnerabilities in My Own AI Agent's Tool Access
stories.author: dannwaneri
bullet_points: The article details the discovery of security vulnerabilities within a self-built AI agent.
The AI agent, named GeoMart, was developed for the OpenAI WebMCP Challenge.
The core topic revolves around securing tool access within custom AI applications.
